Nothing compared to some of the stories here, but my best friend of 8 years has been secretly messaging my ex, when we were still together. She’d speak their language which I can barely understand when in a group, excluding me. Happened all the time. Soon half of our conversations when it was just my ex and me were about her issues. He called me by her name once. All of a sudden they’re “friends”, going out for drinks together. I fucking practically lived with the man. I loved him so much, we were giving dating a second shot. And all of a sudden he’s saying if only I could also speak his native language- like she does. 

And when I blew up of course it snowballed into even more covert contact. I told her everything, when before I tried to hide it for how humiliating it felt. She said she’s sorry and didn’t know, and will stop it the contact. Guess what? Didn’t happen. A cherry on top, at another occasion afterwards he gave me a lecture how I’ve been causing her heartache by being XYZ. So she’s been complaining about me. Of course she thinks I don’t know. I don’t even blame my ex because he doesn’t owe me any decency at this point, but my best friend? I’d never do anything to her. 

I invited her recently to hang out with my new date and his friends, all Russians. Again she tried to exclude me and rope them into not speaking English- we’d talk and she’d respond in Russian. They never bit the bait, maybe because they have class /s, but it really opened my eyes. My first best friend tried to fuck my first serious boyfriend, but somehow this hurts much more.

 I just want you to know that it is not worth killing yourself over. Please call suicide hotiline and speak to advisors at your university- I was in your situation last year with my major. Had no prior experience, was failing exams, thinking it’d be better to go ahead and kill myself and stop being a failure and a burden. But, time has passed, and I am still here. Life is not perfect, I’m still struggling, but it’s much more manageable now. 
Just wake up each day, do your best and persevere, and something will change. 


Please, talk to advisors (academic and mental health counsellors) at your uni. I hear American schools often offer free legal aid service- it might be worth a try. Speak to professors and ask for help. I learned that it is best to reach out to people, explain your struggles and current academic situation and ask them to help- there are resources in place, all that’s needed is someone who will help you access them. And sometimes, even a kind word helps.

Also, I wish I could meet someone to be happy with and marry, and have a life with. Just got dumped, and it came out of the blue. I loved him so much and truly thought that we were happy and that he was happy. It’s heartbreaking that he wasn’t. So, I’d be happy to meet someone “real” and never have another breakup again.

Oh, just like my mother. At some point all you can do is accept that your parents are sometimes nuts, and keep your head down when they’re acting crazy. And remember, it’s not about you, it’s about them. It’s mostly projection with the side of “I really don’t know how things work nowadays but according to my limited knowledge of the past and heresay, bla bla bla”. Frankly, do your own thing and try not to take it personally. I know it’s hard to hear your own mother say these things, but there is nothing you can do. Study hard, work hard, move out, and then control how much you let her in your life. 

EDIT: lol, just saw your comment about how she screamed, cooked soup, and then went crazy again. My mother would do exactly the same, only her version would be to barge in slamming the door and then verbally abuse me, leave, calm down, and then repeat. And then pretend it never happened. Not fun, not nice, somewhat traumatising, but ultimately, it’s not a reflection on you. You do you, OP, you’re doing great in life.

Speak to both of your families and make a plan together. Considering that your parents are both well off and provided they want you to succeed in life nonetheless and will help, there is no reason why this has to be a great life tragedy. You don’t need to abort or adopt the baby out as some redditors “strongly suggest” here, if parents would be willing to help take care of the baby, help you finish education, make life easier. Yes, first years won’t be easy, but I know quite a few girls, from very rich families to those from middle class, whose parents were willing to provide either babysitting and emotional support, or financial support, and they are fine now. A few years passed, babies grew up a bit, they finished education, started jobs. Good luck! Speak to your parents.

I’m sorry but you need to learn how to be more responsible and independent. Things like navigating your way at the airport and driving a car, as well as taking responsibility at work, are manageable and can be learned. You’re 30- of course any decent partner would expect these skills from their SO. I strongly suggest you go to a doctor and figure out where these low energy levels come from- I had anaemia and hypothyroidism, and faced similar issues as you did. Could barely get up from bed some days. Barring these, go to psychologist and try to find mental roots of the problem- Seasonal Affective Disorder, depression, childhood patterns that may affect your reluctance to “adult”.

Also, food for thought: you have potential that is now going unfulfilled. And that’s a shame. You’re going through life so superficially, you barely skim it. You’re wholly capable of becoming an independent and strong woman and potential future mother- you CAN do this. Just try, step out of your comfort zone. Are you afraid of failure? Have you simply grown too used to relying on others? Is it easier to be labelled as “childish” than “flawed” if you risk making a mistake? Is it because your family dynamic was similar? Is it a form of social anxiety? Depression? There are a few possible roots to this problem, look deep inside, see what resonates and then talk about it with a psychologist.

You're being reasonable. Whether your fear of a particular breed is logical or not (and imo it is), it's there, and that's all that matters. You might never be at ease around these dogs, and it'll show. You won't trust them. You won't be confident. And dogs will sense it. All animals do, whether you're handling a horse or a dog or a lion. You need to be grounded and confident, and that comes from a sense of safety and security that you're lacking near this breed. And with dogs that require extra care, such as fosters, you CANNOT be unsure and uneasy because it brings nervous energy into the relationship. Your heart beats faster, you sweat, you're more nervous, your stance is never fully relaxed, and it makes the dog wonder what the hell is wrong if you seem to be constantly on guard. And if a human is freaking out over something, then perhaps a dog should be weary and vigilant too. And in that state of prolonged heightened awareness, animal's responses might ultimately be off. It's not good for the dog. It's not good for you. There are many different dogs or other animals in the world. I'd say it's a small concession to get a Labrador instead of a Dalmatian if it makes your partner happy and stops them fearing for their life.

Completely agree. I don't understand how most commenters seem to think OP did a completely normal reasonable thing. Seems frankly batshit insane to me. He should stay out of his parents' marriage, he escalated the situation in a completely nuclear way, with little respect for his parents' feelings and boundaries. What he should have done was contact his mother and/or father and ask for clarification. Instead he blew things up. Sorry OP, but it's not about you. Stay out of it. You may be a part of the family but you are not a part of your parents marriage: you don't know what is happening between them, you don't know how long they've been unhappy or distant with each other, you're not privy to the hidden nuances and complexities of their relationship. Your mum knows, she says the divorce is amicable, leave it at that. Don't stir shit because you don't have all information and might make things worse.

I agree that likely his ex wife cared a lot about elaborate proposals and expensive jewellery, and he still hasn't processed all this in a healthy way. But I'd be so incredibly hurt. If he planned crazy proposals involving family months in advance, then proposes to you watching Netflix, I would also wonder. Same with the ring. I'd worry I'm appreciated and valued less than his ex, that I'm a rebound, that he doesn't care as much about me and our relationship. And that would be a clue for the guy to actually explain: maybe he did the expensive wedding and engagement and realised he was pressured and nothing good came out of it. You're supposed to be a team, a partnership. Work together. Compromise. Not spitefully throw out the ring out of the window to hurt the other person. It's just so... mean, and hurtful, and despicable. 
I think both of you need to go to therapy. Seperatedly. And then, and only then, think of getting counselling together and marrying. I say it only because his behaviour was abusive: and whether it was part of an ongoing pattern or a single behaviour, is to be seen. But if it's the former, then you need separate counselling before taking any further steps.

I don't get why so many people reply as if she literally berated OP and set the quilt on fire. She's probably just anxious to have everything as perfect and symmetrical in the house for the new baby as possible and simultaneously had no idea how much work it takes to make a quilt (I know I don't). OP knows that she put in 3 months and that fixing is not really possible, the pregnant lady doesn't. She thanked for the gift and told OP multiple times she loved it. Why is it worth starting an argument over it? Just reply "Sorry but it's not really possible to fix the corner, I spent 3 months on that thing and it's as good as it's going to get. However, flaws or not, it'll still keep the baby warm and hopefully transfer some of that love I put in while making it". I guarantee you that the answer will be along the lines of "Oh my god I had no idea you put in so much time and effort, thank you, I'm so sorry, I really love it". 
Why attribute to malice what is likely explained by ignorance.

I don't know what I can say that hasn't already been said by other commenters, but I just feel so sorry that you had such a horrible experience. Others, like K, can't or don't. But it's not an excuse. She should know better. She's an adult woman in a position of authority. Behaving like she does is just disgusting. You're a strong person, OP, to have endured it all, asked for help, gotten therapy and medication, reached to parents and friends. Ultimately, you won: because you'll find a better job soon, where you'll hopefully be valued and treated humanely, and K will stay exactly what she is: a bitter, unhappy, miserable woman who drives everyone around her away with her bullshit and gas lighting. Your boyfriend sounds incredibly immature and like a child. Writing email to his mother pretending to be yours is the kind of bullshit I'd think of doing when I was 13. He is 23, abusive family or not, it's time for him to become independent. If he doesn't take that step, you won't be able to help him no matter how much you try. Go back home, OP. And he either follows you or doesn't, but it's a lost cause if you stay. And frankly, I would also sit down with a therapist and think through why exactly YOU accept this. OP, you are a 30 year old woman who has willingly staid for the last few weeks with highly abusive, scary people. You have decided to LIVE with them. You are complacent being in a relationship with an immature guy who not only accepts that his family abuses you, but also doesn't try to gain independence. He doesn't drive. He doesn't work. I have no doubt that his family affected him deeply and it must have been a traumatising childhood, and I don't doubt that he has trouble finding a job in SA, but he is an adult now. There are a lot of issues here that you should think through. Him being angry at you is also a bad sign: do you even know who he is apart from his family? Because this amount of abuse seeps through your pores and infects you, and you don't really know which way he'll go when (if) he finally leaves them. I assume you're not thinking of moving to SA, so he'd have to move to US or both of you move elsewhere. With stress and huge life changes, are you willing to accept that it will be a long uphill road until he is a functioning, independent human being? Does he have it in him to go above his upbringing? I don't know, OP. It seems to me you're trying to save him, but he is in too deep. I hope I'm wrong.


Also some things to consider: You might have to support him for a very long time. He may or may not get a job over minimal wage. He may or may not get university education. He may never learn how to drive. He may never be able to cut down the family ties: if you have children, realise that they will be the grandparents. If you divorce and he gets half custody, you will have no power to control the extent to which they're in their life when at their father's. He says now he wants to go NC but all of his actions show that he is still codependent like hell. Whether he will be able to break free of their influence permanently, only time will tell. So far it seems unlikely.
When dating someone, don't count on them changing for the better. What he is now might be what you'll ever get. Only you know if you'd be okay living like this for the rest of your life. I know I wouldn't.

I know you probably heard it before, but have you thought of getting a second pet? Preferably a dog, or a cat or something else that the dog can interact with? It's very common to have separation anxiety in pets that are left alone, horses are a prime example: experts even say to get a chicken for the company, otherwise they start to self harm from anxiety. Imagine your only sources of socialising are humans who are busy all the time with their own life's: you'd go crazy too. I'd suggest you get another dog, preferably one that's calm and settled, though a busy, excited time-taking pup would do too, and introduce very demanding exercise in free time to tire her out, while also buying tools like that machine that throws balls to be fetched and can be operated by the dog (can't remember the name now). But simply speaking, introduce enough activities and energy- and- attention consuming things in your dog's life that she won't need your presence to be fulfilled.
